verification_report.summary: The proof is not valid for the main theorem as written. Its first regularity input applies Dang's Theorem A/3.1, but that theorem requires a globally defined density in L^p(X), p>1; the manuscript assumes only that f is smooth and positive on Ω and proves no local Hölder substitute. Smoothness on Ω does not control integrability near X\Ω. Continuing exactly as requested under the additional explicit hypothesis φ∈C^{0,α}_{loc}(Ω), the rest of the proof passes: the nonclosed Bedford–Taylor comparison and convolution steps, exact Guan–Li Dirichlet approximants, polynomial C^4-to-trace boundary estimate, square-root trace peak, regular-set stability, logarithmic/subpower localization, dyadic interpolation, both torsion commutations relating first and second Chern Ricci, the polynomial Calabi/cutoff/rescaling estimate, the C^{1,α}-to-trace iteration, and the final minimization on the nonregular locus are quantitatively consistent. Thus the defect belongs to the broad source statement, not to the repaired local-Hölder version.

critical_errors.issue: Dang Theorem A/3.1 assumes μ=f dV_X with a globally defined f∈L^p(X), p>1. The stated theorem assumes only f∈C∞(Ω), f>0; this need not give any global L^p control near X\Ω, and no applicable local Hölder theorem is proved. Consequently continuity/Hölder continuity of φ—and hence the proper-gap continuity, polynomial boundary smoothing, and all subsequent localization—is unjustified for the theorem as written.

repair_hints: State φ∈C^{0,α}_{loc}(Ω) explicitly (the precise repair used in this audit), or strengthen the density hypotheses so that Dang Theorem A/3.1 genuinely applies—namely a globally defined nonnegative L^p(X) density for some p>1, together with its other hypotheses. With the explicit local-Hölder assumption, no further repair to the audited argument is required.
